descriptors.R: nominee of the party in office since 1921, renominating the sitting President
descriptors.D: nominee of the party out of the presidency since 1921, which won control of the House of Representatives in 1930

compile_desc.D: the party out of the presidency since 1921

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Socialist and a Communist nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Hoover, Roosevelt, Curtis, Garner, Norman Thomas, Foster, Al Smith or Coolidge

slice_sources.men: 1930 and 1940 censuses interpolated to November 1932 (the 1930 "Mexican" race category folded back into white, as the 1940 census recoded it); men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states, citizens only, American Indians included as citizens since the 1924 Indian Citizenship Act (some Western states still barred them in practice); calibrated to certified 1932 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1932, women 21+ outside the South, all enfranchised by the Nineteenth Amendment; turnout from the carried-forward women-to-men ratio, calibrated to each state's 1932 vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1932, white adults (including Mexican-origin adults, listed separately in 1930) in the eleven former Confederate states; poll taxes in most of them; calibrated to certified 1932 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1932, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement by poll tax, literacy test and the white primary continues, so the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1932, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized; no state let aliens vote after 1926.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
the 1928 nominee of the party out of power
